transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Tom Nguyen (SableGrid VP Eng), Leah Foster (Platform Lead), Ben Ortiz (FinOps), Rhea Patel (CTO joined 15m in)

Summary:
Quick ops+finops workshop to prioritize reliability items, review recent cost spikes, and agree on a short pilot to validate dedicated capacity. Customer wants clear runway for fall launch; main constraints are latency SLO degradation during bursts and unexpected token cost variance.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jamie Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off, um, quick agenda — cost breakout, reliability incidents, and then a proposed pilot. Marta, quick note on goal?
[00:15] Marta Ruiz: yeah goal is align on a 2 week action and who owns what, nothing super formal, just, uh, make sure finance and eng are comfortable.
[00:32] Tom Nguyen: thanks. To be clear we saw a 35% cost bump last month, spikes around marketing blast and some nightly batch jobs, and latency SLOs slipped from 120ms to about 450ms for a subset of requests.
[00:48] Aisha Khan: okay, can you share the pattern — is it many small requests or big context ones? sometimes the KV cache prefix hits help, other times long sequences blow the tail latency.
[01:05] Leah Foster: main traffic is 2 types — chat-ish interactive paths at 300 QPS and background summarization jobs at lower QPS but 8k token windows. The summarization runs at night and it seems to blow up costs.
[01:22] Ben Ortiz: from finance side it's the token burn during these long summarizations; the per-token model choice matters. We thought quantized variants would save ~40% but we saw less.
[01:38] Aisha Khan: yeah, quantisation gains depend a lot on sequence length and kernel selection; also our runtime fallback can route to a larger variant if a model is busy — that can cause cost surprises if route policy is set to latency-first.
[01:58] Tom Nguyen: are you suggesting the routing policy might switch them to a larger model automatically? I thought we pinned versions for production.
[02:08] Jamie Park: in this account we saw two incidents where autoscale + fallback routed some traffic to a higher-capacity variant during the marketing window. Pinning is possible — we can set a strict model pin for those routes.
[02:25] Leah Foster: that would help. Also want to understand Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoff. Ben — any constraints?
[02:36] Ben Ortiz: budget wants predictability. If Dedicated gives a clearer monthly commit and lowers unit cost, that's appealing. But we can't overspend the commit. Need a 30-day pilot to measure tail latency under realistic traffic.
[02:52] Aisha Khan: propose 2-hour stress run on a dedicated pool mirroring your traffic profile — we can do a canary and then ramp. We'll instrument per-route token cost, KV cache hit rate, and latency p99 TTL.
[03:08] Tom Nguyen: fine, when can you run it? We need to capture a marketing-like spike too.
[03:14] Jamie Park: schedule as soon as we have the traffic profile from Leah — ideally this week. Lea? (Leah -> Leah/Leah?), sorry — Leah?
[03:24] Leah Foster: yes I'll export the traffic sampling and mark the peak windows, should be able to send it tomorrow EOD.
[03:31] Rhea Patel: (joins) hi sorry I'm late, quick context — as CTO I'm nervous about data residency and audit trails if we move anything off our VPC. How does Redwood handle logging and KMS?
[03:44] Jamie Park: welcome Rhea. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we can push audit logs to your SIEM; for Dedicated we can enable VPC peering and flow logs. I'll share the architecture doc.
[03:58] Rhea Patel: okay share the SOC2 and network diagrams, please. Also, is there RBAC for route-level access? We have teams that shouldn't touch production models.
[04:10] Marta Ruiz: yes RBAC is available, we can show roles in the Console. We'll include that in the doc packet.
[04:18] Ben Ortiz: on the cost spikes — can you show token-level breakdown by route? We saw weird per-route unit differences.
[04:27] Aisha Khan: yes, we'll export a 90-day token-level CSV with route, model, seq length buckets, and cost. Note that transcriptions sometimes mislabel model family names (e.g., 'redwood-neo' might appear as 'redwood-nio' in raw logs) so human review helps.
[04:46] Tom Nguyen: haha okay noted. On reliability, the p99 in that incident was from small chat sessions, not the big summarizers — weird.
[04:56] Leah Foster: small sessions had a cold start effect, plus there was a KV cache low hit rate because keys were slightly different per user. We need prefix canonicalization.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: canonicalization is a good call; our Optimize tool has suggestions for batching and prefixing — we can provide a config snippet to normalize keys and increase prefix hits.
[05:21] Tom Nguyen: can that be done app-side quickly? Or do you need code changes on our end?
[05:26] Aisha Khan: mostly app-side — a few lines to canonicalize user ids and session tokens before they hit the cache. We can provide the snippet and a short script to simulate.
[05:35] Ben Ortiz: for the Dedicated pilot, what are the cost expectations vs hosted? ballpark numbers will help us decide commit size.
[05:44] Jamie Park: high level — Dedicated typically lowers per-token cost 20-45% depending on utilization and quantization. For your workload with heavy long-sequence summarizers, the per-token advantage is larger if you run quantized models and tune batching. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:59] Rhea Patel: security question — how are logs handled during pilot? We can't have PII in vendor logs.
[06:07] Marta Ruiz: we support redaction at ingest and can route raw logs to your long-term storage. We'll include the redaction checklist in the packet.
[06:18] Tom Nguyen: great. Next, roadmap — we need features: better tracing per-request, and an alert if cost per-route deviates >15% week-over-week. Is that on your roadmap?
[06:30] Aisha Khan: yes anomaly alerts and per-route billing dashboards are in the Console roadmap; we can prioritize shapes for enterprise customers. We'll raise this with product.
[06:39] Leah Foster: timeline? We need something before our fall launch (mid-October).
[06:44] Jamie Park: we can fast-track an alert prototype and a dashboard widget by end of September if prioritized.
[06:52] Ben Ortiz: ok that is helpful. On the audit and procurement side — procurement asked for contract SLAs about p99 latency; what do your SLAs look like for Dedicated?
[07:03] Jamie Park: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency SLO targets; we can share the SLA doc and map it to your routes. There's also automatic fallback policies to keep apps online in case of contention.
[07:16] Tom Nguyen: last time fallback swapped us to a different model family and our outputs changed a bit — can you enforce semantic consistency during fallback?
[07:26] Aisha Khan: we can configure fallback chains that limit to model families with matching n-gram and tokenizer profiles to reduce drift; we can produce a regression test harness that runs a small eval suite pre-and-post fallback.
[07:40] Leah Foster: that would be huge — we need to avoid quality regressions.
[07:46] Jamie Park: action — we'll run a small eval with your prompts during the stress run to watch for drift.
[07:52] Marta Ruiz: I'll capture that as an action.
[08:00] Tom Nguyen: timeline recap?
[08:04] Jamie Park: Leah sends traffic profile by 2026-08-21, Aisha delivers cost CSV by 2026-08-24, Jamie shares SOC2 + private deployment checklist by 2026-08-21. Then stress run week of 2026-08-24 or sooner, follow-up triage week of 2026-08-31.
[08:22] Ben Ortiz: can we get a price estimate for a 3-month Dedicated commit if we see 30% cost savings? rough numbers only.
[08:31] Jamie Park: yes we'll include a scenario table in the spreadsheet — commit sizes vs per-token rates and projected savings based on utilization buckets.
[08:41] Rhea Patel: one more — data residency: do you have EU-only logging option? Our EU customers require logs and keys in EU.
[08:51] Marta Ruiz: yes, we have region-restricted deployments and can use EU-managed KMS. We'll document that.
[08:59] Tom Nguyen: ok good. any blockers on your side?
[09:03] Leah Foster: no blockers once we share the traffic. We might ask for a short runbook for the app-side canonicalization change.
[09:11] Aisha Khan: we'll add the snippet and a small test harness.
[09:16] Jamie Park: perfect. let's close with a short recap and owners.
[09:20] Marta Ruiz: recap: 1) Leah provides traffic profile [Leah], 2) Redwood sends 90-day cost CSV and scenario spreadsheet [Aisha/Jamie], 3) schedule 2-hour stress run on Dedicated with eval harness [Aisha/Jamie/Leah], 4) share SOC2/KMS/network docs [Jamie], 5) follow-up triage week of 2026-08-31.
[09:40] Tom Nguyen: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:44] Rhea Patel: thanks — quick note: please flag any legal/contract items early to Ben.
[09:49] Ben Ortiz: will do.
[09:52] Jamie Park: thanks everyone, we'll send the packet and invite for the stress run.
[09:57] meeting end
